_baseline.note: T3 baseline for Alphabet (CIK 1652044). FIRST fiscal year carrying AI-harm/algorithm risk-factor language = FY2018 10-K (accession 0001652044-19-000004, goog10-kq42018.htm, filed 2019-02-05): 'new products and services, including those that incorporate or utilize artificial intelligence and machine learning, can raise new or exacerbate existing ethical, technological, legal, and other challenges, which may negatively affect our brands and demand for our products and services and adversely affect our revenues and operating results.' This generic AI/ML ethical/reputational risk factor persists FY2019 (0001652044-20-000008, goog10-k2019.htm), FY2020 (0001652044-21-000010, goog-20201231.htm), FY2021 (0001652044-22-000019), and FY2022 (0001652044-23-000016, goog-20221231.htm). It MATURES into explicit generative-AI harmful-content language in the FY2023 10-K (0001652044-24-000022, goog-20231231.htm, filed 2024-01-31): 'Our evolving AI-related efforts may give rise to risks related to harmful content, inaccuracies, discrimination, intellectual property infringement or misappropriation, defamation, data privacy, cybersecurity, and other issues'; '...could subject us to competitive harm, regulatory action, legal liability... and brand or reputational harm'; 'Unintended consequences, uses, or customization of our AI tools and systems may negatively affect human rights, privacy, employment, or other social concerns...'. Item 3 Legal Proceedings / Legal Matters note is antitrust-dominated (Epic v. Google, DOJ/state antitrust, EC) and names NO lawsuit/regulatory action tied to any incident in this batch => no T2. Bard appears only as routine product description ('Bard allows users to collaborate with experimental AI...'); Waymo+recall appears only in FY2024/FY2025 10-Ks (outside every incident window) => no T1. Every incident below has an in-window 10-K carrying same-family AI/ML risk language, so T3 floor applies; none rise to T1/T2, none fall to T4.

305.evidence: Window 2019-02-01 to 2020-02-01. In-window FY2018 10-K (0001652044-19-000004, filed 2019-02-05) carries AI/ML ethical/brand risk language; FY2019 10-K (0001652044-20-000008, edge) continues it. YouTube's recommendation algorithm driving misinformation is squarely within the 'AI/ML raise ethical challenges... negatively affect our brands' family. No filing names this advocacy-group allegation; Legal Matters is antitrust-only; 'recommendation' full-text hits are proxy/board noise.
specific_queries: efts q="recommendation" forms=10-K,10-Q,8-K ciks=0001652044 -> only proxy/board-recommendation hits, no YouTube-algorithm litigation
305.rationale: Recommendation-algorithm harm covered by generic AI/ML risk factor; event not named; no legal proceeding disclosed.
